channel.title: Clisa Geopolitics
channel.description: A geopolitical dashboard analyzing Northeast Asian security, great-power competition, and conflicts in Europe and the Middle East from South Korea’s vantage point. Each issue comes with a situation assessment, a strategy evaluation, what it means for people, and probabilistic forecasts.

item.title: Briefing · October 10, 2026
item.description: After Trump-Putin call, U.S. temporarily eases sanctions to let Russian diesel flow · Saudi-led coalition launches major operation against Houthis, says 136 military targets destroyed · Tanker hit off UAE coast catches fire, blaze extinguished · Ethiopia's foreign minister accuses Eritrea of 'all-out invasion,' invokes self-defense

item.title: Features · What it took for a country to invent an alphabet
item.description: For Hangul Day, a third feature, "What it took for a country to invent an alphabet," looks at where the two conditions behind King Sejong's 32-year reign came from, why they lasted only a generation, and what the same question means for the Korean Peninsula in 2026.

item.title: Briefing · October 9, 2026
item.description: Russian guided bombs hit two buses in Kramatorsk, killing 33 · Trump says the U.S. will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterms · Seoul to recall its ambassador to Ukraine · Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, debris hits kindergarten · Accounts mount that Eritrean troops have crossed into Tigray

item.title: Briefing · October 8, 2026
item.description: Russia pounds Ukraine in nationwide missile and drone strike, killing at least 28 · Tanker hit in the Persian Gulf north of Qatar, with casualties reported · Saudi aviation authority says Houthi airport attacks killed 3, injured 36 · IEA members agree to speed up emergency oil releases, prioritizing diesel · Unification Minister Chung Dong-young says a U.S.-North Korea summit could take up reconfirming the demarcation line

item.title: Briefing · October 7, 2026
item.description: Russia hits Kyiv with missiles before dawn on October 7, killing two · North Korea's Foreign Ministry calls Seoul's mine findings a farce, rules out talks with the South on military sovereignty · Drones hit two merchant ships in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, sinking one · Ukraine launches mass drone attack on Moscow area; two killed in surrounding region · Foreign Minister Cho Hyun says Ukraine's apology falls somewhat short, weighs recalling ambassador · Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a ballistic missile aimed at Khamis Mushait

item.title: Briefing · October 6, 2026
item.description: Joint Chiefs conclude North Korean troops planted DMZ mine, blow up mines in first removal · Turkish-owned grain ship sinks after drone attack in Romania's exclusive economic zone · Russian glide bombs kill six, wound 59 in Kharkiv · Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan activate "collective deterrence measures" over Houthi attacks, deploy forces to Saudi Arabia · Yemeni government forces claim to retake Mocha, launch "strategic offensive" toward Sanaa

item.title: Forecast review · October 5 · 4 revised, 2 unchanged
item.description: Last week the United States sent more forces to the Middle East, raising the military pressure on Iran, and North Korea fired a hypersonic intermediate-range missile while rejecting inter-Korean contact. The probabilities of four forecasts were adjusted, and two forecasts with conflicting factors were left unchanged.

item.title: Briefing · October 5, 2026
item.description: North Korea fires hypersonic intermediate-range missile 13 days after last launch · Zelensky says U.S. has proposed trilateral technical-level talks by end of October · Russia strikes Kyiv bridges for fourth straight day · Iran holds to seven conditions for reopening the strait; Trump: "the easy way or the hard way" · Houthis claim strike on Saudi Aramco sites; Saudi-led coalition calls claim "misleading"

item.title: Features · South Koreans' well-being hangs by a thread
item.description: A second feature based on population projections, "South Koreans' well-being hangs by a thread," has been published. The October 1 feature has been retitled "The security vacuum the Korean Peninsula can expect in the 2030s."

item.title: Briefing · October 3, 2026
item.description: U.S. sends carrier group and Marines to Middle East; Trump says war will end "right after the election" · Kim Yo Jong again denies blame for mine blast, rules out "the slightest space or room" for ties with Seoul · Russia launches massive strike on Ukraine's energy facilities ahead of winter · G7 agrees to release 100 million barrels of oil reserves

item.title: Briefing · October 2, 2026
item.description: Trump says stepping up Iran strikes after midterms is "possible" · Lee urges North Korea to restore dialogue in Armed Forces Day speech · Russia warns it would use "all its arsenal, including nuclear weapons" if Kaliningrad is blockaded · U.S. officials see Chinese invasion of Taiwan before 2028 as unlikely · Pakistan launches airstrikes on Afghanistan's Kunar and Helmand provinces

item.title: Features · The security vacuum the Korean Peninsula can expect in the 2030s
item.description: One key assessment and four forecasts (f54–f57) were added to the Korean Peninsula issue. They address the mismatch between the pace at which the United States is handing South Korea primary responsibility for deterring North Korea and the pace at which South Korea is acquiring the means to carry that responsibility.

item.title: Briefing · October 1, 2026
item.description: Defense minister says he believes North Korean troops crossed the MDL to lay mines · Cabinet approves special bill on nuclear-powered submarines · Iran says it has received U.S. reply to its proposal to end the war · U.S. completes troop withdrawal from Iraq · Russia hits power grid around Kyiv ahead of winter

item.title: Briefing · September 30, 2026
item.description: Kim Yo Jong claims DMZ mine blast was staged by Seoul · Russian drone strike sets Kyiv's Academy of Sciences ablaze · U.S. sanctions Iran's arms procurement network even as it talks of renewed negotiations · Hormuz traffic rises, but Brent tops $105 a barrel

item.title: Briefing · September 29, 2026
item.description: Investigation finds DMZ blast very likely caused by North Korean mine · North Korea declares at the U.N. that its nuclear status is irreversible · U.S. demands that nuclear issue be addressed in indirect talks with Iran · Russia sets its biggest defense spending increase since the invasion for 2027 · China Coast Guard announces "routine law-enforcement patrols" east of Taiwan · U.S. and China agree to keep discussing further extension of tariff truce
